_comment: The review card both plugins show when Sentrook asks before a tool call. Hermes shows one text (`hermes`); OpenClaw a title and a description (`openclaw`). For each case both plugins must produce exactly this from `response`, `tool`, `relaxed` (a block a snooze turned into a review), `strong` (absent or false elsewhere; with `relaxed`, the beta snooze of a block with a strong signal: the reasons line says "Would be blocked because" and the answer line warns), `hint` (the suggested grant as the grant command would accept it), `remember` (approving always sets it) and `why_id` (the scan's request id; null when the traffic log is off). `session` (Hermes only, absent or null elsewhere) says what Hermes's Session answer covers: `parties` (later calls in the chat of the same kind, about the same parties, scoring no higher) or `exact` (only this exact action); with a suggested grant the owner's answer sets, one line names it for Session and Always. Budgets: Hermes 300, counted as UTF-16 units after HTML escaping (its Discord card cuts the text at 300, Telegram's at 500 escaped); OpenClaw 80 for the title and 500 code points for the description (it refuses an approval over 80 or 512, and refusing blocks the call). When a card does not fit, what the call does gives way first, then the second reason, then the grant command (pointing to `why`). `errors` are the cards for a call that could not be scanned, by cause.
